title: Protocols to monitor TFEB activation following lysosomal damage in cultured cells using microscopy and immunoblotting
protocol: Seed cells onto plates.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18-24 hours at 37°C.
Prepare LLOMe containing culture medium (final concentration is 1 mM).
Ensure that LLOMe dissolved in EtOH completely before use.
Wash the cells with PBS once.
Add LLOMe containing medium to the cells, incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Remove the medium from the cells.
Wash the cells gently with PBS once.
Add fresh medium to the cells, incubate for 3 hours at 37°C.
Mix 2 μL beads and 1 μL Effectene transfection reagent in 100 μL Buffer PC.
Incubate transfection reagent-coated beads for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Add 1 mL growth medium to the bead mixture.
Remove the medium from the cells.
Add the bead mixture to the cells.
Incubate the cells for 3 hours at 37°C in a CO2 incubator.
Wash the cells with PBS twice to remove attached beads.
Coat coverslips with collagen diluted by 10 times with sterile water.
Place coated coverslips into a sterile cell culture plate.
Incubate the plate at least 30 minutes at 37°C.
Seed cells onto collagen-coated plates.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours at 37°C.
Treat the cells with lysosomal damage-inducing reagents as described in step 2a or 2b.
Wash the cells with PBS once.
Fix the cells with ice-cold 4% PFA.
Incubate the cells for 20 minutes at 20–25°C.
Wash the cells with PBS twice.
Permeabilize the samples with a 50 μg/mL Digitonin-PBS solution for 10 minutes at 20–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Incubate the samples with 0.1% gelatin-PBS for 30 minutes at 20–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Incubate the samples with primary antibodies (anti-Gal3 and anti-Lamp1 antibodies) diluted in 0.1% gelatin-PBS for 1 hour at 20–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Incubate the samples with secondary antibodies diluted in 0.1% gelatin-PBS for 40 minutes, in the dark at 20–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS and ddH2O three times (PBS twice → ddH2O once).
Mount the samples with a drop of mounting media containing DAPI onto glass slides.
Remove excess media and seal the coverslips with nail polish.
Observe the samples by confocal microscopy.
Place sterile coverslips into a sterile cell culture plate.
Coat coverslips with Cellmatrix diluted by 10 times with sterile water.
Incubate the plate at least 30 min at 37°C.
Wash coverslips with PBS twice.
Seed cells onto collagen-coated plates.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours at 37°C.
Induce lysosomal damage using LLOMe or beads transfection as described in step 2a or 2b.
Wash the cells with PBS once.
Fix the cells with ice-cold 4% PFA.
Incubate the fixed cells for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the samples with PBS and ddH2O three times (PBS twice, ddH2O once).
Mount the samples with a drop of mounting medium containing DAPI onto glass slides.
Remove excess media from the slides.
Seal the coverslips with nail polish.
Observe cells using widefield fluorescence microscopy.
Take images of the cells for DAPI and TFEB channels.
Quantify the nucleus/cytoplasm ratio of TFEB using CellProfiler software.
Identify regions of cells from smoothed TFEB images.
Name identified cell regions as <Cells>.
Match primary objects with secondary objects and name matched primary objects as <filtered Nuclei>.
Identify the cytoplasm by subtracting nuclei objects <filtered Nuclei> from cell objects <Cells>.
Name identified cytoplasm regions as <Cytoplasm>.
Measure intensity of TFEB in <filtered Nuclei>.
Measure intensity of TFEB in <Cytoplasm>.
Divide the mean intensity of <filtered Nuclei> by the mean intensity of <Cytoplasm>.
Seed cells to a sterile cell culture plate.
Incubate the cells with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours at 37°C.
Treat the cells with LLOMe or transfection reagent coated beads.
Wash the cells with ice-cold PBS twice.
Suspend the ice-cold cells in 200 μL M-PER mammalian protein extraction reagent containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors for total cell lysate.
Incubate cell lysates for 10 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 15,000 × g for 10 minutes and collect the supernatant.
Add the 5× SDS sample buffer to the supernatant.
Boil the samples for 5 minutes at 95°C.
Use the samples for standard method of SDS-PAGE and western blotting.
Suspend the ice-cold cells in 300 μL PBS containing 0.1% NP-40, protease, and phosphatase inhibitors as lysis buffer.
Incubate cell lysates for 10 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 9,100 × g for 10 seconds and take 100 μL supernatant (cytosolic fraction).
Remove the supernatant and wash the pellet with 300 μL PBS containing 0.1% NP-40.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 10,000 rpm for 10 seconds and remove supernatant.
Add 200 μL PBS containing 0.1% NP-40 (nuclear fraction) to the pellet.
Mix with 5× SDS sample buffer.
Boil the nuclear fraction for 5 minutes at 95°C.
Load equal amounts (about 20–30 μg of total protein) of sample and molecular weight marker into the wells of an 8% polyacrylamide SDS-PAGE gel.
Run the gels for 1–1.5 hours at 20 mA per mini gel.
Transfer the proteins from the gel to a polyvinylidene fluoride membrane.
Incubate the membranes with blocking solution (TBST containing 1% skim milk) for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate the membranes with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Wash the membranes with TBST (5 min ×3).
Incubate the membranes with HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies diluted 5,000× in blocking solution for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the membranes with TBST (5 min ×3).
Detect immunoreactive bands using luminescent reagents on a ChemiDoc Touch imaging system.
